ai.description: Theloderma baibungense is a 30–35 mm frog with a dark brown dorsum featuring irregular light spots. It is distinguished by a granular, warty skin texture and distinct webbing between the toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Theloderma baibungense* is best distinguished by the presence of distinct, large, raised, ivory-white tubercles scattered across its otherwise dark, mottled dorsal skin.
ai.habitat: *Theloderma baibungense* inhabits subtropical evergreen broad-leaved forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Theloderma baibungense is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged against mossy surfaces during the day to evade predators through crypsis.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Theloderma baibungense* is an oviparous breeder that deposits small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Theloderma baibungense* is found in the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh, specifically within the Eastern Himalayas at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Theloderma baibungense* produces a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard calling from tree holes or water-filled cavities in dense forests.
